about.title: Santa Monica Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Monica is a small city by Los Angeles County standards—about 93,000 residents—yet its clinics, surgical centers and emergency rooms see a steady flow of patients from across the Westside. Some arrive after collisions on Lincoln Boulevard or the I-10; in 2025 alone, 572 people were injured in 445 crashes here, and many of them passed through a local emergency department. Most of that care is careful. When it isn't, the harm can be lasting. Medical malpractice in California means a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that lapse caused injury—a disappointing result by itself does not qualify. Proving the difference almost always takes a qualified medical expert reviewing your records. Deadlines are tight under MICRA: generally one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened, with a 90-day notice sent before any lawsuit is filed. We handle these claims on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Monica Patients Choose Us

items.title: MICRA's clock is short and unforgiving
items.desc: You generally have one year from discovering the injury, and no more than three from when it occurred, plus a 90-day notice must go out before suit. Getting started early protects those dates.

items.title: Expert review, not guesswork
items.desc: California courts nearly always require a qualified medical expert to explain how care fell below the standard. Our team knows how to line that up before deadlines pass.

items.title: A rising cap, understood correctly
items.desc: MICRA limits non-economic damages, but that cap increases every year and does not touch medical bills or lost income. We can explain what applies to your situation—without promising a number.

items.question: I had a bad surgical outcome at a Santa Monica hospital. Is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not automatically. California law asks whether the provider's care fell below what a reasonably careful professional would have done, and whether that failure caused your harm. Complications can happen even with proper care. A medical expert's review of your chart is usually what settles the question.

items.question: How long do I have to act in Los Angeles County?
items.answer: MICRA sets the timeline statewide: generally one year from when you discovered, or should have discovered, the injury, and never more than three years from the date it happened. A 90-day pre-suit notice must also be served before filing. Because those windows can close faster than people expect, reaching out early matters.

items.question: Do you charge me anything for a free case review?
items.answer: No. Our service is free. We work on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless your claim results in a recovery.
